entries.clue: Yes, you’re plugging USB into box the wrong way round (6-2)

entries.clue: Police force uniform with number at bottom of sleeve and number at the top? (5,4)

entries.clue: 28 shillings (3)

annotation.definitionNote: '28' points to the answer at 28 across, a SLEDGE; and 'bob' can stand for 'shillings' because the slang word takes no plural, as in 'ten bob'.

blocks.note: 28 across is SLEDGE, so this definition asks for a kind of sledge
old British slang for shillings, a word that stayed the same in the plural

annotation.walkthrough: A bare number points to another answer, here 28 across. BOB is short for bobsleigh, and 'ten bob' meant ten shillings.
annotation.definitionFit: A bob is short for bobsleigh, a racing sledge; and 'bob' was slang for the shilling, a coin worth a twentieth of a pound before 1971.

entries.clue: Extremist members of cult radicalised (5)

entries.clue: Show of peace and love left bad vibe on farm (5,6)

entries.clue: Hold surgery up by four seconds to swallow last bite of cake (7)

entries.clue: Muscular editor lifts great weight (5)

entries.clue: A thousand ducks quacked excitedly, having united north of the Channel (8)

entries.clue: Model greeting bishop in doorway perhaps (7)

hi is a greeting

entries.clue: Cleaning up liquid sink has in it (5,2)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Cleaning up' pretends to be washing-up, but it means making a lot of money. QUID is slang for a pound.

entries.clue: Freaking out divides upset followers (9)

the letters of OUT rearranged

entries.clue: Entering with pun, sorry (not sorry) (11)

blocks.note: the word taken as it stands, to be mixed
the word taken as it stands, to be mixed

annotation.walkthrough: 'Sorry' appears twice. The first one scrambles the letters, and the bracketed 'not sorry' is the definition.

entries.clue: English people finally translated Polish text (5)

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
men are people
the last letter of translated

entries.clue: Big flower left by German escort (5)

annotation.surface: An enormous bloom left behind by a German companion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is read as flow-er: something that flows, not a bloom. A gusher is an oil well or spring that shoots up.

entries.clue: Glow bug by rocks starts to combust eventually (9)

the first letters of combust and eventually

entries.clue: Delivery recipient must pay for port fees, unfortunately (8)

entries.clue: As Spooner sings hackneyed song, somewhere to relax (4,5)

entries.clue: Quiet men, trembling, holding quiet instruments (9)

entries.clue: Never sin, put back fruit (5)
